项目摘要
中文摘要:

数据隐私是神经网络技术健康发展的重要保障，隐私计算可在保护数据机密性的前提下，提供敏感数据运算功能，有效平衡数据隐私性和可用性之间的矛盾。但目前神经网络隐私计算存在安全假设较强、扩展性不足、难以支持复杂训练模型等问题。本项目拟利用零知识混淆电路、承诺不经意传输、带验证秘密共享、同态加密等密码技术，研究抗强攻击者的多方神经网络隐私计算。主要研究内容包括:1）研究大整数域和比特域安全多方计算基础部件，设计安全耦合的运算域转换模块；2） 构造支持不同神经网络预测和训练模型的多方隐私计算方案，满足恶意敌手模型下的可证明安全性；3)实现基于标准数据集的多方神经网络隐私计算实例化方案，开展正确性和性能测试。本项目兼顾安全、隐私、效率等实际应用需求，力图打破数据壁垒，发展数据流动中的隐私保护理论，健全神经网络数据安全防护体系，为大规模数据应用提供理论基础和技术支撑。
Abstract:

Data privacy is the cornerstone for the healthy development of neural networks. The privacy-preserving calculation can protect the confidentiality of data while providing the functionality of computing over sensitive data, balancing the contraction between data privacy and data usability. Drawbacks in existing solutions include strong security assumptions, low extensibility, and being challenging to support complicated training algorithms. Therefore, this project focuses on the multi-party privacy-preserving neural network against strong adversaries, potentially using cryptographic technologies involving zero-knowledge garbled circuit, committed oblivious transfer, authenticated secret sharing, homomorphic encryption, and so on forth. Specifically, 1) we will first study secure multi-party calculation toolkits over arithmetic and bool fields, and secure conversion models between different fields; 2) We will construct multi-party privacy-preserving computing schemes for prediction and training algorithms of different neural networks, and formally prove the security against the malicious adversary; 3) We will implement the privacy-preserving neural network schemes based on standard test datasets, and consequently test the correctness and performance. Taking into consideration practical requirements, e.g., security, privacy, efficiency, etc., this project aims to break the data island and develop the privacy protection theory in the data flow. The results of this project will lay a critical theoretical foundation on the data privacy of neural networks and provide efficient technical support for the healthy development of large-scale data applications.

Abstract (Brief description of research background, main methods, contributions, and research data):

This project addresses two core scientific problems: the organic integration of multi-party computation (MPC) building blocks across heterogeneous computation domains and the decoupled optimization paradigm for privacy-preserving computation execution and verification, involving four key scientific questions in total. The research is carried out along three main directions: (1) privacy-preserving MPC building blocks for multi-party neural networks against malicious adversaries, (2) secure MPC protocols for multi-party neural network computation under malicious security, and (3) system-level simulation and evaluation of privacy-preserving multi-party neural network computation based on standard benchmark datasets. The project has produced a series of efficient MPC techniques supporting diverse neural network models, including verifiable computation, privacy-preserving data acquisition, and large-scale data fusion computation. These results significantly enhance the data privacy protection capability of neural network models and ensure secure and controlled data circulation. Since the project initiation, 10 high-quality papers have been published in leading journals and conferences in related areas, including 9 papers in IEEE Transactions journals and CCF-recommended journals or conferences. In addition, 2 national invention patents have been filed, one of which has been granted. The research team has also contributed to the training of 6 Ph.D. students and 9 master' s students. The project has achieved key breakthroughs in privacy-preserving multi-party neural network computation and system design against strong adversaries, promoting national innovation in data security and supporting the secure and controllable development of artificial intelligence industries. The research has progressed as planned, successfully completed all tasks, and achieved the expected objectives.
